With this notebook, I plan to download chemical data from watina,
cross compute differences,
and quantify variogram parameters
to estimate spatial similarity range.


# Chemical Data
## rationale/demarcation
The measurement intervals and data structure of hydrogeographical and chemical data in `watina` are fundamentally different, and justify separate investigation.
In particular:

- Temporal sampling: water levels are monitored quasi-continuously (ideally), whereas chemical measurements happen twice a year at best.
- Chemistry: water levels are one simple measure, whereas chemistry comes as a set of multiple compoud classess.
- Methodology: there are detection limits on the chemistry side, and known pressure/level interdependencies (e.g. well/seepage areas) on the physical side.
- Recurrency: both measurement types show recurrent structure, which might be linked, but not directly.


Herein, I focus on chemistry, and more specifically on the following compound classes:

- \(NO_3\)
- \(NH_4\)
- \(PO_4\)

We will not regard \(NO_2\).

I will query pairs of (approximately) simultaneously sampled sites and quantify differences of measurement outcome, depending on site distance. 
And then we'll see.


## glimpse at the database
To create the query below, knowledge of the database structure is beneficial.

The `dimDatum` table:
```{r eval=FALSE}
glimpse(DBI::dbGetQuery(watina_dwh,
  paste0("
    SELECT *
    FROM dimDatum
      ")
  ))
```

I will use `Jaardag_Nummer/365.0 + Jaar` for restricting time difference.


<br>
The `dimPeilpunt` table:
```{r eval=FALSE}
glimpse(DBI::dbGetQuery(watina_dwh,
  paste0("
    SELECT *,
        SUBSTRING(PeilpuntCode, 1, 4) AS region
    FROM dimPeilpunt
      ")
  ))
```

I will use `SUBSTRING(PeilpuntCode, 1, 3) = GebiedCode` equality for restricting spatial distance.



<br>
The `dimGebied` table:
```{r eval=FALSE}
glimpse(DBI::dbGetQuery(watina_dwh,
  paste0("
    SELECT *
    FROM dimGebied
      ")
  ))
```

-> `GebiedCode` can be used to join locs afterwards.



<br>
The `dimChemVar` table:
```{r eval=FALSE}
head(DBI::dbGetQuery(watina_dwh,
  paste0("
    SELECT ChemVarWID, ChemVarNaam, ChemVarEenheid, Ion
    FROM dimChemVar
      ")
  ), 32)
```

-> holds both the ID and the name of compounds; either can be used (6 = \(PO_4\), 7 = \(NO_3\), 8 = \(NO_2\), 9 = \(NH_4\)).

## data query
There are existing `watina` functions for chemical data.
However, in my experience, SQL is efficient at cross-joining large tables.

Therefore, I will use a direct query to get the difference-distance data.

This includes several filters:

- maximal sampling interval: 30d
- maximal filterdepth difference: 0.5m
- ChemVar listed above 
- validation VLD, SDV, UNK


```{r, eval=TRUE}

load_raw_data <- function () {
  DBI::dbGetQuery(watina_dwh,
    paste0("
      SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT
          CHM1.region AS region,
          CHM1.ChemVarWID AS chemvar_id,
          CHM1.ChemMetingWID AS id1,
          CHM1.pp_code AS pp1,
          CHM1.filterdepth AS z1,
          CHM1.MetingStatusCode AS status1,
          CHM1.DatumWID AS date1,
          CHM1.time AS t1,
          CHM1.Meetwaarde AS mw1,
          CHM2.ChemMetingWID AS id2,
          CHM2.pp_code AS pp2,
          CHM2.filterdepth AS z2,
          CHM2.MetingStatusCode AS status2,
          CHM2.DatumWID AS date2,
          CHM2.time AS t2,
          CHM2.Meetwaarde AS mw2
        FROM (
          SELECT
              FactChemischeMeting.*,
              Jaardag_Nummer/365.0 + Jaar AS time,
              SUBSTRING(PeilpuntCode, 1, 3) AS region,
              (PeilbuisLengte - ReferentieNiveauMaaiveld - (FilterLengte/2)) AS filterdepth,
              dimPeilpunt.PeilpuntCode AS pp_code
          FROM FactChemischeMeting
          LEFT JOIN dimDatum ON FactChemischeMeting.DatumWID = dimDatum.DatumWID
          LEFT JOIN dimPeilpunt ON FactChemischeMeting.PeilpuntWID = dimPeilpunt.PeilpuntID
          ) CHM1
        LEFT JOIN (
          SELECT
              FactChemischeMeting.*,
              Jaardag_Nummer/365.0 + Jaar AS time,
              SUBSTRING(PeilpuntCode, 1, 3) AS region,
              (PeilbuisLengte - ReferentieNiveauMaaiveld - (FilterLengte/2)) AS filterdepth,
              dimPeilpunt.PeilpuntCode AS pp_code
          FROM FactChemischeMeting
          LEFT JOIN dimDatum ON FactChemischeMeting.DatumWID = dimDatum.DatumWID
          LEFT JOIN dimPeilpunt ON FactChemischeMeting.PeilpuntWID = dimPeilpunt.PeilpuntID
          ) CHM2
          ON (CHM1.ChemVarWID = CHM2.ChemVarWID)
         AND (CHM1.region = CHM2.region)
        WHERE CHM1.ChemVarWID IN (6, 7, 8, 9)
          AND CHM2.MetingStatusCode = CHM1.MetingStatusCode
          AND (CHM2.time - CHM1.time) < (30.0/365)
          AND ABS(CHM2.filterdepth - CHM1.filterdepth) <= 1.0
          AND (CHM2.ChemMetingWID != CHM1.ChemMetingWID)
          AND (CHM1.PeilpuntWID < CHM2.PeilpuntWID)
          AND CHM2.DatumWID >= CHM1.DatumWID
          AND CHM1.MetingStatusCode IN ('VLD', 'SDV', 'UNK')
        ) AS ChemRepeated
      LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT
          ChemVarWID,
          ChemVarCode AS compound,
          ChemVarEenheid AS unit
        FROM DimChemVar
        ) AS DCV
        ON DCV.ChemVarWID = ChemRepeated.chemvar_id
        ")
    ) %>% select(-ChemVarWID)
}

```

## double-joining locs
Comparing two locations, I will join the locs twice: once to every location in the pair.
Then, distances and differences are computed, and relevant entries filtered.
Finally, factors are generated from categorical variables.

```{r}
data <- data_raw %>%
  left_join(
    select(locs, obswell_code, x, y),
    by = join_by(pp1 == obswell_code),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>% rename(c("x1" = x, "y1" = y)) %>%
  left_join(
    select(locs, obswell_code, x, y),
    by = join_by(pp2 == obswell_code),
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) %>% rename(c("x2" = x, "y2" = y)) %>%
  filter_at(
    vars(x1, x2, y1, y2, z1, z2),
    all_vars(!is.na(.))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    dx = sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2),
    dt = sqrt((t2-t1)^2),
    dz = z2-z1,
    dmw = mw2 - mw1,
    dmw_log = log(abs(dmw)+1.0),
    dmw_rel = (mw2 - mw1) / (abs(mw1) + abs(mw2))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(compound == "N-NO2"),
    dx > 0,
    dx <= 100,
    abs(dmw) <= 10
  ) %>%
  mutate_at(
    vars(
      region,
      chemvar_id,
      status1,
      status2,
      compound,
      unit
    ), as.factor
  )

```


```{r}
data %>%
  summarize(cnt = n(), .by = c(compound))
```

## soilclass
```{r}
soilmap_raw <- load_zenodo_data('soilmap')

soilmap <- soilmap_raw %>%
  transmute(
    soilclass = case_when(
      str_detect(bsm_mo_tex, "V") ~ "peat",
      str_detect(bsm_mo_tex, "^U") ~ "heavy",
      str_detect(bsm_mo_tex, "[SZPLX]") ~ "light",
      str_detect(bsm_mo_tex, ".+") ~ "heavy",
      .default = "unknown"
    ) %>%
      factor()
  )

```



```{r}
loc_p1 <- st_join(
  data %>%
    as_points(xvar = "x1", yvar = "y1", warn_dupl = FALSE),
  soilmap
  ) %>%
  mutate(soilclass = tidyr::replace_na(soilclass, "unknown")) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(soilclass) %>%
  rename(soilclass1 = soilclass)

loc_p2 <- st_join(
  data %>%
    as_points(xvar = "x2", yvar = "y2", warn_dupl = FALSE),
  soilmap
  ) %>%
  mutate(soilclass = tidyr::replace_na(soilclass, "unknown")) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(soilclass) %>%
  rename(soilclass2 = soilclass)

data <- cbind(data, loc_p1, loc_p2)
```

# Modeling in variograms

I guess it is time to squeeze the last out of this data set with a complex model.

Question: What is the concentration difference `dmw`, its log `dmw_log`, or relative concentration difference `dmw_rel` between two sites, given:

- ~~chemical `compound` (random effect)~~
- inter-sampling interval (`dt`)
- filter depth difference (`dz`)
- ~~`soilclass` (random effect)~~
- distance (`dx`), obviously.

*UPDATE 1: I did not get the models I liked with `brms`, and went to `rstan`.*
*UPDATE 2: random effects were disregarded to reduce power loss due to data fragmentation.*

```{r}
library("rstan")
library("shinystan")
```


```{r}
data <- data %>% mutate(
  dc = (dmw_rel + 1.0)/2.0,
  compound_id = as.integer(compound)
  )
glimpse(data)
```

```{r}
data_onecompound <- data %>% filter(
  dmw_log > 0,
  # dx <= 25,
  compound == "N-NH4"
  # compound == "N-NO3"
  # compound == "P-PO4"
  )
glimpse(data_onecompound)
```

## Less Guessing, More Thinking (LGMT) Model

- https://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/modeling-a-continuous-0-1-variable/18468/4
- https://mc-stan.org/docs/functions-reference/positive_continuous_distributions.html
- https://mc-stan.org/docs/functions-reference/distributions_over_unbounded_vectors.html#multi-student-t-cholesky-fun


considerations:

- Using relative difference might not be a good idea.
- Using absolute difference is required (`dmw`; yet note that the distribution is crappy).
- Difference makes "zero" a valid outcome; in fact, zero is a very likely case (although, maybe not; this might depend on detection limit).


strategy:

- Plot data distribution again. Try transforming \(dc\) = concentration difference 
- Start with only `data_onecompound`, for simplicity: the compounds' concentration differences are independent for all practical purposes, no need for a compound model.
- Try lognormal, because why not. Otherwise go exponential (maybe "plus a Gaussian" for the wobbling).
- Model structure: \(d\xi \sim lognormal(a + b1 dx + b2 dz )\); optionally add (+ b3 dt)


`stan` notes (still learning!):

- `transformed parameters {...}` are parameters, i.e. their samples are added to the output
- brackets are very mandatory, e.g. `inv_logit(intercept + X * slopes);` is wrong and needs to be `inv_logit(intercept + (X * slopes));`
- TODO Is it possible to pass in prior values (e.g. pass global mean as intercept)?


```{stan eval=FALSE, output.var="explorative_model"}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;               // sample size
  matrix[N, 3] X; // predictors: distance, depth
  real prob[N]; // outcome variable
}

parameters {
  vector[3] slopes;
  real intercept;
  real<lower=0> residual;      // residual variability / model error
  // real<lower=0> dof;      // the "nu" parameter for Student's T (degrees of freedom)
}

model {
  // priors
  slopes ~ normal(0, 0.1);
  intercept ~ normal(0, 1);
  residual ~ cauchy(1, 1);
  // dof ~ normal(5, 10);

  // "posterior", "likelihood", give it a name...
  // prob ~ normal(intercept + (X * slopes), residual); // mu, sigma
  prob ~ lognormal(intercept + (X * slopes), residual); // mu, sigma

  // prob ~ student_t(dof, intercept + (X * slopes), residual); // nu, mu, sigma
}
```

```{r}
explorative_model <- stan_model(
  file = "./explorative_model.stan",
  model_name = "explorative model"
  )
```


```{r}
exploratory_model_fit <- sampling(
  explorative_model,
  list(
    N = nrow(data_onecompound),
    prob = data_onecompound$dmw_log,
    X = cbind(
      abs(standardize(data_onecompound$dx)),
      abs(standardize(data_onecompound$dz))
      )
    ),
  iter = 2048,
  chains = 6,
  cores = 6
  )

names(exploratory_model_fit)[1:2] <- c("slope_dx", "slope_dz") # , "slope_dt"
                                  
# print(exploratory_model_fit)
```


```{r eval=FALSE}
launch_shinystan(exploratory_model_fit)
```

Notes:

- Non-Representative success with **model on \(NH_4\)**: 
  - **clear effect of depth difference**; 
  - **no effect of distance**
  - large residual variation, weird intercept
  - convergence: yes; checks good; using standardized data
  - "zero difference" had to be excluded (`lognormal` requirement)
  - \(NH_4\) works with Student T posterior; the others don't converge; yet `lognormal` preferred
- Effects on \(NO_3\) or \(PO_4\): 
  - none, really
  - even larger intercept and residual

General note:

- model building was far too erratic; this is not a conventional linear relation.

There was a bug due to failed joins, producing missing data.
It turned out to be related to `filterdepth` automatically excluded by the `get_locs()` function.


```{r eval=FALSE}

  filter(region == "VOT") %>%
  summarize(
    count = n(),
    .by = c(pp1, status1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(pp1)
head(test_data, 10)
```


```{r eval=FALSE}
test_locs <- locs %>%
  filter(area_code == "VOT") %>%
  select(obswell_code, loc_code, x, y) %>%
  arrange(obswell_code) 
head(test_locs, 10)
```
- ~~`test_locs` does not contain `BUIP003X`~~

```{r eval=FALSE}
head(test_data %>%
  left_join(
    test_locs,
    by = join_by(pp1 == obswell_code)
  ) %>% summarize(
    count = n(),
    .by = c(pp1, loc_code)
  ), 16)
```


- `pp1` from `data_raw` comes directly from `dimPeilpunt`, joined to `dimChemischeMeting`.
- `loc_code` in `locs` comes from `vwDimMeetpunt` (`loc_type == P`!), on which we join `vwDimPeilpunt` (`PeilpuntStatusCode IN (VLD, ENT, CLD)`)
- Other Filters in `get_locs`:
  - `PeilpuntOpenbaarheidTypeCode` / `OpenbaarheidWID`
  - `PeilbuisLengte`, `FilterLengte`, `ReferentieNiveauMaaiveld`
  - `filterdepth_range` was the killer!

```{r eval=FALSE}
head(DBI::dbGetQuery(watina_dwh,
  paste0("
    SELECT
        MeetpuntCode,
        PeilpuntCode,
        MeetpuntTypeCode,
        MeetpuntStatusCode,
        MeetpuntXCoordinaat,
        MeetpuntYCoordinaat,
        OpenbaarheidWID,
        PeilpuntStatusCode,
        COUNT(PeilpuntWID) AS cnt
    FROM dimPeilpunt AS PPT
    LEFT JOIN dimMeetpunt AS MPT
      ON MPT.MeetpuntWID = PPT.MeetpuntWID
    WHERE PeilpuntCode LIKE 'VOT%'
    GROUP BY
        MeetpuntCode,
        PeilpuntCode,
        MeetpuntTypeCode, 
        MeetpuntStatusCode, 
        MeetpuntXCoordinaat,
        MeetpuntYCoordinaat,
        OpenbaarheidWID,
        PeilpuntStatusCode
    ORDER BY PeilpuntCode ASC
      ")
  ), 10)
```

## Intermediate, Working Models

### beta distribution
#### plain beta
```{stan eval=FALSE, output.var="explorative_model_plain"}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;                  // sample size
  real<lower=0, upper=1> dc[N]; // outcome variable
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> beta_a;         // posterior dist parameter alpha
  real<lower=0> beta_b;         // posterior dist parameter beta
}

model {
  // priors
  beta_a ~ cauchy(0.0, 1.0);
  beta_b ~ cauchy(0.0, 1.0);

  // "posterior", "likelihood", give it a name...
  // https://mc-stan.org/docs/functions-reference/continuous_distributions_on_0_1.html#beta-distribution
  dc ~ beta(beta_a, beta_b);

}

```


#### beta - compound "intercept"
```{stan eval=FALSE, output.var="explorative_model_randomintercept"}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;               // sample size
  int<lower=1> J;               // number of compounds
  int<lower=1, upper=J> chem[N]; // chemical ID id
  real<lower=0, upper=1> dc[N]; // outcome variable
}

parameters {
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[J] u; // chem intercepts
  real<lower=0> kappa_u;         // chem kappa
  real<lower=0> kappa_beta;         // ...
}

model {
  real estimator;

  // priors
  kappa_u ~ cauchy(0.0, 2.0);
  u ~ beta_proportion(0.5, kappa_u); //chem random mean
  kappa_beta ~ cauchy(0.0, 2.0);

  for (i in 1:N){
    estimator = u[chem[i]];

    // "posterior", "likelihood", give it a name...
    dc[i] ~ beta_proportion(estimator, kappa_beta);    //
  }

}

```


#### compound slope and intercept
```{stan eval=FALSE, output.var="explorative_model_compound"}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;               // sample size
  int<lower=1> J;               // number of compounds
  int<lower=1, upper=J> chem[N]; // chemical ID id
  real<lower=0, upper=1> dc[N]; // outcome variable
  real<lower=0, upper=100> dist[N]; // predictor: distance
}

parameters {
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[J] u; // chem intercepts
  vector[J] v;                   // chem slopes
  real<lower=0> kappa_u;         // chem kappa
  real<lower=0> sigma_v;         // chem kappa
  real<lower=0> kappa_beta;      // ...
}

model {
  real estimator;

  // priors
  sigma_v ~ cauchy(0.0, 0.2);
  v ~ normal(v, sigma_v); //chem slope mean
  kappa_u ~ cauchy(0.0, 2.0);
  u ~ beta_proportion(0.5, kappa_u); //chem intercept
  kappa_beta ~ cauchy(0.0, 2.0); // model residual

  for (i in 1:N){
    estimator = u[chem[i]] + v[chem[i]] * dist[i];

    // "posterior", "likelihood", give it a name...
    dc[i] ~ beta_proportion(estimator, kappa_beta);    //
  }

}
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
  list(N = nrow(data),
       dc = data$dc,
       J = length(levels(data$compound)),
       chem = data$compound_id,
       dist = data$dt
       ),
```



### Beta - inv logit matrix
... I ended up here, because I wanted to have `beta` posterior, but `linear model mean`-like behavior.
```{stan eval=FALSE, output.var="beta_inv_logit_model"}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;               // sample size
  matrix[N, 2] X; // predictors: distance, depth
  real<lower=0, upper=1> prob[N]; // outcome variable
}

parameters {
  vector[2] slopes;
  real intercept;
  real<lower=0> kappa;
}


// transformed parameters get displayed (element-wise) in the output.
//transformed parameters {
//  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] estimator; // => moved to "model"
//  estimator = inv_logit(intercept + (X * slopes));  // ! brackets!
//}

model {
  // priors
  slopes ~ normal(0, 1);
  intercept ~ normal(0, 1);

  kappa ~ gamma(1, 1); // model residual

  // "posterior", "likelihood", give it a name...
  prob ~ beta_proportion(inv_logit(intercept + (X * slopes)), kappa);    //

}
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
explorative_model <- stan_model("./explorative_model.stan")
exploratory_model_fit <- sampling(
  explorative_model,
  list(N = nrow(data),
       prob = data$dc,
       X = cbind(data$dx, data$dz)
       ),
  iter = 1000,
  chains = 6,
  cores = 6
  )
                                  
print(exploratory_model_fit)
```


### Students' T distribution
*no convergence guaranteed.*

```{stan eval=FALSE, output.var="studentt_nonconvergent_model"}
data {
  int<lower=1> N;               // sample size
  matrix[N, 3] X; // predictors: distance, depth
  real prob[N]; // outcome variable
}

parameters {
  vector[3] slopes;
  real intercept;
  real<lower=0> residual;      // residual variability / model error
  real<lower=0> dof;      // the "nu" parameter for Student's T (degrees of freedom)
}

model {
  // priors
  slopes ~ normal(0, 0.1);
  intercept ~ normal(0, 1);
  residual ~ cauchy(1, 1);
  dof ~ normal(5, 10);

  // "posterior", "likelihood", give it a name...
  prob ~ student_t(dof, intercept + (X * slopes), residual); // nu, mu, sigma

}
```
